extracted.intended_audience: people who need to convert lengths between metric and imperial units (students, DIYers, engineers, general public)
extracted.subtask_short: convert centimeters to feet and inches
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step guide to convert a length in centimeters into feet (decimal) or into a feet-and-inches representation, including the exact formula, procedural steps, rounding guidance, worked examples, and a conversion chart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centimeters to feet conversion formula
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since there are 30.48 centimeters in one foot, you can use this cm to feet formula to convert. Example: feet = (170 cm ÷ 30.48) = 5.577428 ft, so 170 cm in feet is 5.577428.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to convert cm to feet and inches (stepwise)
rubrics_metrics.description: To convert cm to feet and inches, follow these steps: Step 1: Begin with the cm to feet conversion above to get the resulting feet in decimal form first. Step 2: Take the number to the left of the decimal as the number of whole feet. Step 3: Take the number to the right of the decimal point and convert it to inches (multiply by 12). Step 4: Round that result to the nearest whole number to get the number of inches. Step 5: Combine the number of whole feet and inches to get your final answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example converting 170 cm: 170 cm ÷ 30.48 = 5.577428 ft; 0.577428 × 12 = 6.929136; round to nearest whole number → 7 inches; result: 170 cm ≈ 5 ft 7 in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert decimal remainder to inches
rubrics_metrics.description: Take the decimal remainder of the feet value and multiply it by 12 to convert to inches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 0.577428 (decimal remainder) × 12 = 6.929136 inches (before rounding). This is the standard step because there are 12 inches in one foot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Round inches to the nearest whole number
rubrics_metrics.description: Round the converted inches result to the nearest whole number to obtain a convenient feet-and-inches measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the example 6.929136 rounds up to 7 inches. Because rounding is performed, the page uses an 'approximately equal' sign rather than an exact equals sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use approximate symbol when rounding
rubrics_metrics.description: When rounding during conversion, denote the result with an 'approximately equal' sign rather than an exact equal sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that we use an 'approximately equal' sign instead of an equal sign as we performed some rounding of the measurement since 170 centimeters is not exactly equal to 5 feet, 7 inches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use inch fraction calculator for fractional inches
rubrics_metrics.description: If you need fractional-inch precision rather than rounded whole inches, convert decimal inches to fractional inches via an inch fraction calculator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page links to an inch fraction calculator to convert decimal to fractional inches if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate conversions with a height converter
rubrics_metrics.description: You can validate the feet-and-inches conversion result using the site's height converter tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page suggests using the height converter to confirm results (no further technical detail provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Centimeter definition and equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: One centimeter is equal to one-hundredth (1/100) of a meter and is equal to 0.393701 inches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The meter is defined as the distance light travels in a vacuum in 1/299,792,458 of a second. Metric rulers typically have 30 cm. To get a rough idea of 1 cm, a standard number 2 pencil is about 1 cm thick.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foot definition and equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: A foot is equal to 12 inches or 1/3 of a yard; one foot is equal to 0.3048 meters because the international yard is defined as exactly 0.9144 meters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feet abbreviations: 'ft' or the prime symbol (′) or single-quote ('). Feet are US customary and imperial units. Measurements in feet commonly use a 12" ruler or tape measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to use physical measuring tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a ruler or tape measure for measuring length in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulers are available in imperial, metric, or combination types—make sure you get the correct type for your needs. The page also offers free downloadable and printable rulers including imperial and metric measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a conversion chart of common values
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a table mapping common lengths in centimeters to their equivalent heights in feet and feet+inches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists many example conversions (e.g., 170 cm → 5.5774 ft → 5 ft 6.9 in) and notes that a more comprehensive height comparison chart is available.
